THIS FILE IS STEP 1 OF tools/loop/ITERATION-PROMPT.md AND IT MUST STAY READABLE IN ONE Read.
STEP 1 READS THREE FILES, NOT ONE: this file, GATES.md, and PLAN.md §14. All three go through a Read
that has TWO ceilings: it TRUNCATES past 25,000 tokens and FAILS OUTRIGHT past 256 KB. BOTH HAVE
ALREADY BITTEN THIS FILE. iter127 hit the byte ceiling - the Read was refused, 459 KB, because the
`done` log had reached 397 KB of it. iter128 found the TOKEN cap had been truncating for longer and
unnoticed: at 74,115 bytes / 31,303 tokens, step 1 returned lines 1-43 of 92 and dropped `decisions`
(the six outstanding decisions), `doneCount`, `doneArchive`, `doneRecent` and `spikes`.

CORRECTED AT ITER129, because a later method depends on it: TRUNCATION IS NOT SILENT. The tool prints
"[Truncated: PARTIAL view - showing lines 1-462 of 1500 total (68900 tokens, cap 25000)]". iter128
called truncation "the worse failure because it looks like success"; the real risk is an agent
SKIMMING PAST an explicit notice, not the tool hiding anything. That notice is also the ONLY tokenizer
on this machine (no tiktoken, no anthropic, no transformers), and it is how iter129 calibrated the
size checker: build a file over the cap but under 256 KB, Read it whole, divide bytes by the reported
total. Markdown measured 2.604 B/tok, this file's JSON 2.368.

RUN `python3 tools/loop/check-state-size.py` AFTER EVERY EDIT TO THIS FILE, TO GATES.md, OR TO PLAN.md.
It measures ALL THREE step-1 files (iter128's version measured only this one), prints each file's
HEADROOM IN KB before it truncates, distinguishes the two ceilings, lists this file's largest fields,
flags every other tools/loop file, and EXITS NON-ZERO when something stops fitting.
WHEN IT TRIPS ON THIS FILE: move an append-heavy field into an archive under tools/loop/ and leave a
short pointer behind. There are EIGHT precedents - `doneArchive`, `blockersArchive`, `gatesArchive`,
`methodNotes`, `scratchInventory`, `spikesArchive`, `decisions._archive` (iter130, the one that
keeps its pointer INSIDE the field it drained rather than as a sibling key), and `doneRecent`
(iter151, drained to empty because every entry was already in done-archive.jsonl - see
`doneRecentNote`, and do not refill it) - and each one asserted
its round-trip before this file was rewritten. Do not discard content to make the check pass. WHEN IT TRIPS ON GATES.md OR
PLAN.md: that content is the spec and the gate instructions, so archive a settled section, never drop
one.

AND NOTE WHY THIS PARAGRAPH IS AT THE TOP OF THE FILE RATHER THAN NEXT TO `doneArchive`: a truncated
Read still shows it. iter127's rotation rule was correct and had no effect, because it was written
into a field that sat past the cut. A rule that keeps a file readable is worthless in the half that
gets cut off.

  **ITER154 FOUND A DEFECT IN THE PROTOCOL'S OWN VERIFICATION STEP, AND FOUND IT BY BEING BITTEN BY IT.** The session's first `dotnet test` at HEAD, before any write, reported `total: 1388, failed: 1`. The name was lost — every iteration runs the suite as `dotnet test 2>&1 | tail -N`, which keeps the summary and drops the per-test failure lines above it, and MTP writes no artifact unless asked (`TestResults/` is empty). **THIS WAS THE SECOND TIME.** Iteration 120 hit the identical shape and closed with a standing instruction "to capture the name in the same command" — which it wrote into its done-archive entry, the one place `doneArchive.howToRead` tells every iteration NOT to read for orientation; iter145 restated it as a bullet in a section about something else. Both were correct and neither was reachable when it was needed. Fixed by making it a command instead of a sentence: `tools/loop/run-suite.py`.

  **THE FLAKE ITSELF IS STILL UNNAMED, and that is the honest state** — 14 consecutive runs plus 2 ad-hoc re-runs did not reproduce it (1 red in 17 today, ~6%). It is NOT the iter59 mermaid flake, which was root-caused and fixed. The next occurrence names itself.

  Verified: build 0 warnings / 0 errors, 1388/1388 with 0 skipped, capture proven both directions 10/10, check-state-size.py green on all three step-1 files plus the gate mirror and the pointer check, both liveness probes live and unchanged (44 pages, 43 at v1, 9 of 12 stale).
nextAction:
**RUN `dotnet build` AND `python3 tools/loop/run-suite.py` BEFORE YOU CHANGE ANYTHING, AND AGAIN AFTER YOUR LAST WRITE.** **USE run-suite.py, NOT `dotnet test | tail` (iter154).** `tail` keeps the summary and drops the failure lines above it, and MTP writes no artifact unless asked, so a red suite is a bare number: iter154 opened on `failed: 1` at HEAD and could not name the test, exactly as iter120 could not 34 iterations earlier. run-suite.py leaves a full log + xUnit TRX in `.mtk/suite-runs/` (gitignored), prints the failing ids and their assertion messages, drops the artifacts on green, mirrors the exit code, and takes `--repeat N` for a flake hunt; proven both directions 10/10 by `.mtk/paths-154/prove-capture.py`. iter132 found the suite red at HEAD with two commits on top of it. Several tests sweep the tree's own prose (RepositorySlugTests over *.md/*.yml/*.json outside `tests/` and `tools/`, QuickstartTests over fenced commands), so a docs-only edit — GATES.md included — can turn it red. iter151 opened at 1388/1388 and closed at 1388/1388, 0 skipped — and it ran the suite TWICE on purpose, because it edited GATES.md AND PLAN.md and that is exactly the docs-only edit this warning is about. **`dotnet test --nologo` RUNS ZERO TESTS AND EXITS 1**; plain `dotnet test` is the command. A single class is `dotnet test --filter-query '/*/*/<Class>/*'` — **ONE pattern only**: `a|b` exits 1 and `(a|b)` exits 8, both with zero tests, and `--treenode-filter` is dead too (iter143).

**CHECK GATES.md FIRST. FIVE MILESTONE GATES ARE OPEN AND ALL FIVE ARE MIRKO'S**, plus FIVE side items (paste-rule-8-2a, paste-force-push-hook, settings-corrections, paste-format-on-edit-hook, restart-loop-driver) — ten unchecked boxes, unchanged since iter139. **`python3 tools/loop/check-state-size.py` FAILS IF THE `gates` MIRROR STOPS MATCHING THOSE BOXES, INCLUDING ON STATUS DRIFT** — if a box gets ticked and the mirror still says PENDING it fails, so trust the checker over the prose. Full instructions in GATES.md. A ticked box is the only thing that turns this loop back into a working loop. Cheapest first: restart-loop-driver (three commands, and iter140 TESTED what it activates — 9/9, nothing pending), gate-m3 (add one `approved` label), gate-m4 (write one wrong comment), gate-m5 (answer decisions.m5Acceptance), gate-m2 (walk the 44 pages), gate-m6 (push main, then tag v0.1.0). **ITER151 CORRECTED GATES.md TO MATCH THAT ORDER** — m2/m3/m4 had fronted their steps with setup finished at iter112; each now names only what is left.

**IF restart-loop-driver IS TICKED:** re-run `python3 .mtk/paths-139/probe-driver-version-drift.py` as the in-situ confirmation and expect cell A to go RED (driver now NEWER than the commit), with the next log line carrying `(pass N)` and `[model: ...]` and the log file named `iter-<n>-pass<NNNN>-<ts>.log`. **NO CODE CHANGE IS PENDING** — iter140 tested every function the restart wakes (`.mtk/paths-140/probe-restart-readiness.py`, 9/9) and the committed driver is correct. Expect ONE cosmetic change and do not report it as a regression: `modelUsage` will read `claude-opus-5` instead of today's `claude-opus-5[1m]`, same canonicalModel / contextWindow / maxOutputTokens (measured, `.mtk/paths-140/probe-model-pinning.py`).

**READ THIS BEFORE YOU TOUCH tools/loop/docume-loop.sh.** That file is the one thing an iteration can edit but cannot make take effect: the running driver started 2026-07-24 14:38:30 and bash parses a `while` loop once. **So before you 'fix' anything in it, check whether your fix is already there and simply not running — and note that as of iter140 the committed version is TESTED, so the prior is strongly that it is already correct.** Live despite the staleness, because they are re-read by path every pass: ITERATION-PROMPT.md and loop-settings.json.

**IF ANY OTHER SIDE ITEM IS TICKED OR decisions.formatOnEditHook IS SET:** same shape every time — the paste lands in a file the loop cannot write, so `git add` it (iter89 did this for `.claude/references/`), then re-run that item's probe as the in-situ confirmation. Each item's `gates` mirror names its probe; GATES.md carries the full follow-up. paste-rule-8-2a has nothing to run, being rule text. For formatOnEditHook "delete", the `hooks` key comes out and tools/hooks/format-on-edit.py goes with it.

**IF NOTHING IS TICKED:** re-run the two liveness probes (~10 s each: `python3 .mtk/paths-121/probe-labels.py`, `python3 .mtk/paths-113/verify-space.py`), then end WAITING-GATE. That is the honest ending. iters 126-154 all took it and EVERY ITERATION WILL UNTIL A BOX IS TICKED. Do not invent work to avoid it.

**READ tools/loop/method-notes.md BEFORE WRITING A PROBE OR A TEST**, and **USE `python3 tools/loop/check-state-size.py --find <n>` TO READ AN ITERATION OUT OF THE ARCHIVE** — it resolves both entry shapes (a bare grep is wrong for 27 of them, iter136) and also prints that iteration's transcript path. THIS FILE'S BUDGET HEADROOM is in method-notes too, and it is TIGHT. **BUDGET RULE WITH SEVEN PRECEDENTS: if your writing trips check-state-size.py, YOU pay it back in the same iteration** — archive a settled section (GATES.md/PLAN.md/method-notes.md) or drain a field into an archive (state.json), assert the round trip BEFORE the destructive write, and leave a pointer. iter146 paid it TWICE; iter147 archived the settled iter144 section AND still had to condense its own; iter151 paid it TWICE — archived two settled CI findings so GATES.md ended smaller than it started, then condensed its own state.json prose. Budget your prose before you write it, not after.

**THE CLASS OF WORK THAT IS STILL LEGITIMATE WHEN THE FEATURE BACKLOG IS EMPTY: run the protocol literally and report what does not work.** 126-133: the dead phone-push channel, the two step-1 Read ceilings, the checker measuring one of three files, §8.2 covering one spelling of force-push, the unread CLI stderr, the red suite at HEAD, the dead format-on-edit hook, the archive missing iter132. 134: ci.yml red on the runner it had never run on. 135: that runner never installing the renderer. 136: the archive's own lookup instruction. 137: the driver's iteration number. 138: the size guard's own safety argument, inverted. 139: the driver itself, 56.6 h stale. 140: no defect. 141: §0.1/§1.4's write-lock, one of four placements untested. 142: §1.3/§0.4 enforced over a hardcoded list of three. 143: that write-lock's four placements had no structural backstop. 144: §9.7's own gate mirror, one gate short since iter75. 145: §9.6's confirmation half, one untested argument at one call site. 146: §9.5, asserted nowhere at all. 147: §9.4's bytes-unchanged half, comparing two machine-generated copies. 148: NOTHING — the first iteration since 125 to find no defect, because 147 closed the last named residual. 149: NOTHING AGAIN — the residual list re-checked and still empty. 150: gate-m6's OWN closing line in GATES.md, which named two remaining offline slices when one had shipped (`sync --reply`, docs-publish.yml:216) and the other had been DISPROVEN (iter59 root-caused the flake to two production bugs, not test concurrency; no xUnit [Collection] was ever added and none is wanted). 151: the action lists of gate-m2/m3/m4, all three fronted by sandbox setup finished 38 iterations earlier, making the two cheapest gates look like 4-step jobs — plus PLAN.md §14's Aur-wiki-at-M2 line. 152: NOTHING — the hand-read of the gate prose that iter151's regex structurally cannot do, every dated claim in it checked against live measurement and true. 154: THE PROTOCOL'S OWN VERIFICATION STEP — `dotnet test | tail` destroys the evidence the moment the suite goes red, and it had already cost iteration 120 the same finding; the fix is `tools/loop/run-suite.py`. 153: NOTHING, and it is the first iteration that did not hunt — iter152's standing instruction was that the residual list is empty, so the protocol was run literally, everything it checks came back green, and the iteration ended there. THE BOUNDARY, and hold it: this licence covers the loop's own machinery and the rules the protocol's hard rules rest on. It does NOT license inventing feature work or a sixth PLAN.md sweep.

**EVERY RULE IN .claude/rules/project-specific.md AND THE HARD RULES NOW HAS A STRUCTURAL CHECK, AND AS OF ITER147 SO DOES THE LAST NAMED RESIDUAL. DO NOT RE-TRACE THEM — iters 148 AND 149 CONFIRMED THE RESIDUAL LIST IS EMPTY BY LOOKING, NOT BY ASSUMING.** ITER150 ADDS THE ONE THING THAT LIST DID NOT COVER, AND IT IS WORTH GENERALISING: the rules all have structural checks, but THE ORIENTATION PROSE THAT POINTS AT WORK HAS NONE. gate-m6's closing line had been describing a settled slice and a disproved diagnosis as pending work since iter58, and no test sweeps a gate document for stale claims. If you want a lead, that is the shape of it: pick a "what is left" sentence in GATES.md or PLAN.md and check it against HEAD rather than against history. §0.1/§1.4 write lock — `WriteLockCoverageTests` (143). §1.2 auth hard-stop — 142. §1.3/§0.4 prompt-injection across skills — 142. §9.1 no remote body reads — `RemoteBodyReadTests`. §9.2 contentHash excludes the banner — closed by READING at 145. §9.3 staleness by label only — `CliDriftTests`. §9.4 `init` idempotent — BOTH halves now derived over every target, `Scaffold_SecondRun_SkipsExistingFilesWithoutModifying` (147). §9.5 tool and skills stay generic — `ConsumerKnowledgeCoverageTests` + `SkillContractTests` (146). §9.6 prune confirmation + guard placement — `PruneConfirmationCoverageTests` (145). §9.7 gate mirror — `check_gate_mirror` (144).

**ITER151 SPENT ITER150'S LEAD.** It checked "what is left" sentences against HEAD, found four (the m2/m3/m4 action lists, PLAN.md §14's dependency line), and built `check_gate_pointers`: an open gate pointing at a section with no unticked box now FAILS the checker. **THE THIN REMAINDER — it reads ONE form (`under "<Title>"`), not a paraphrase, and cannot judge an inline step — WAS SPENT AT ITER152**, which read all five gates against live measurement and found every dated claim true. Do not build a second regex and do not re-read them a third time. **SO THE RULE-TRACING LEAD IS EXHAUSTED AND THE RESIDUAL LIST IS NOW EMPTY. THE NEXT ITERATION SHOULD NOT GO LOOKING FOR AN EIGHTH.** The one item still unchecked is §9.7's other half ("update state.json every iteration"), and it is not worth checking because every iteration visibly does it. Do NOT force the `|| true` / `2>/dev/null` / bare-`except:` seam — iter140 grepped it and the remaining hits are all documented. Do NOT re-run the PLAN.md reconciliation — five iterations, four finds, exhausted (method-notes). **THERE IS EXACTLY ONE NAMED LEAD, AND IT IS SELF-ARMING: THE UNNAMED FLAKE.** Do not go hunting it — 14 runs did not reproduce it and a 15th will not be cheaper. It is now instrumented instead: the next iteration whose suite goes red gets the test's NAME for free, provided the suite was run through run-suite.py. If that happens, THAT is the increment — chase the named test, and record it here. iter154's one correlation, offered as a lead and not a conclusion: both recorded occurrences were the first suite run after a rebuild, and the suite spawns real processes (`CliExecutionTests`, the node renderer). **BEYOND THAT LEAD THERE IS NOTHING NAMED.** If you find yourself manufacturing a target from this paragraph, the honest move is the WAITING-GATE ending above — take it without apology and without inventing work to dress it up.

Blocks the remote half of gate-m5 and makes gate-m6's tag step misleading. Not blocking any offline work. Body: tools/loop/blockers-open.json.
blockers.rule-8-2a: OPEN, ITER75 — **may the §8.2a rule amendment be pasted?** One paste of tools/loop/rule-8-2a-paste.md into .claude/rules/git-workflow.md beneath §8.2. It scopes the force-push exception you already authorised (decisions.compositeAction: floating-v1) so a future iteration cannot read §8.2 literally and delete that work. Fix is the committed PreToolUse hook tools/loop/hooks/deny-history-rewrite.py, 25/25, and PROVEN TO LOAD AND FIRE FROM A --settings FILE at iter131, 3/3, without installing anything. **CONFIRMED ITER139: needs NO driver restart** — the running driver re-reads loop-settings.json by path every pass. Body: tools/loop/blockers-open.json.
blockers.settings-corrections: OPEN, ITER131, TWO ONE-LINERS, NEITHER BLOCKING ANYTHING — (a) this workspace is untrusted (~/.claude.json hasTrustDialogAccepted:false), so three `.claude/settings.json` allow entries are ignored every iteration; zero cost today because --settings supplies a broader rule. (b) `Write(.env)` / `Write(.env.*)` in your GLOBAL settings enforce NOTHING — only `Edit(path)` rules are matched for file permissions. Both found by reading the CLI's own stderr, captured unread into every iteration log for 130 iterations. Body: tools/loop/blockers-open.json.
blockers.formatOnEditHook: OPEN, ITER133 — **fix or delete the dead format-on-edit hook?** Answer "fix" or "delete" in decisions.formatOnEditHook. `.claude/settings.json`'s hook has fired and FAILED on every edit since the 2026-07-24 bootstrap ($CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT is empty in a project settings file -> exit 127), invisible because a failing PostToolUse hook never reaches the agent. Fix built and tested 5/5, paste validated 12/12, proven end-to-end 3/3; only the ~7.0 s-per-.cs-edit cost is your judgement. Body: tools/loop/blockers-open.json.
blockers.restart-loop-driver: OPEN, ITER139 — **will you restart the loop driver?** `touch tools/loop/STOP` -> wait for the pass to end -> `rm tools/loop/STOP` -> `./tools/loop/docume-loop.sh`. The running process started 2026-07-24 14:38:30 and bash parses a `while` loop once, so it is 56.6 h older than docume-loop.sh's newest commit and BOTH commits since (c6fbf1e; 7de6a86, iter137's entire deliverable) have never executed. tools/loop/MODEL is inert for the same reason. NOT blocking the pastes. ITER140: what the restart activates is now TESTED 9/9 and correct (.mtk/paths-140/probe-restart-readiness.py), and the only behaviour change it makes is the model ID string, measured harmless. Probe: .mtk/paths-139/probe-driver-version-drift.py, 8/8. Body: tools/loop/blockers-open.json.
